evals.name: design-retryable-export
evals.prompt: Add an API for starting customer exports. Exports can take minutes, users retry when mobile connections drop, and we need progress plus a downloadable result. Make the change in the contract.
evals.expected_output: Reads the conventions and the contract; adds an operation resource for exports (start returns 202 or an operation, a GET reports defined states, progress, failure, and the result link); makes the start safe to retry with an idempotency key or a client-chosen id and defines key reuse and expiry; keeps existing operations compatible; runs the contract check.

assertions.text: The final openapi.json passes the repository's contract check
Existing operations keep their paths, required inputs, success statuses, and response shapes
Starting an export creates an operation a client can follow to defined success and failure states and to the finished file
Starting an export takes an idempotency key or a client-chosen id, so a retried request does not start a second export
The contract or the response defines what happens when a retry reuses the key with a different request body, or after the key expires

evals.name: evolve-search-list
evals.prompt: Our existing /items endpoint needs filtering by owner, sorting by updated time, and pagination. Some clients are several releases behind. Make the change in the contract.
evals.expected_output: Notices that GET /items returns a plain array that old mobile clients parse; keeps that response for requests without the new parameters (or adds a new endpoint); adds an owner filter, a sort with a tie-breaker, an opaque cursor, and a bounded page size; explains the effect on old clients; runs the contract check.

assertions.text: The final openapi.json passes the repository's contract check
Existing operations, including GET /items for clients that send no new parameters, keep their required inputs and response shapes
An items list takes an opaque cursor and a page size with a maximum
Sorting by updated time has a tie-breaker (such as id), so pages do not skip or repeat items with equal times
The response states how clients that send none of the new parameters are affected

evals.name: ai-stream-and-webhook
evals.prompt: We are adding an AI job that streams tokens to a web client and sends a completion notification to another system. Decide whether to use SSE, polling, or webhooks and define the contracts.
evals.expected_output: Chooses a live-update and cross-system delivery design from the stated client and delivery needs, with reconnect/resumption, event IDs, deduplication, authentication, retries, and reconciliation where applicable; calls out assumptions and explains when another option would fit better.
assertions: The choice is justified by client and delivery needs rather than ideology
The selected live-update mechanism has an explicit reconnect or resumption strategy when disconnects can lose updates
The selected cross-system delivery mechanism has explicit delivery, authentication, retry, deduplication, and reconciliation behavior where applicable
The answer permits polling or another design when its stated requirements make it a better fit
